name: Aktru Glaciers
full: The Aktru river valley on the northern slope of the North Chuya Range, 30–33 km south of the Chuysky Trakt at the village of Kurai (turn-off at about km 826). A glacier cluster of 7 glaciers (~16 km²): Left (Big) Aktru, Right Aktru, Maly Aktru and others; in the valley — the Aktru alpine camp (since 1938), the Altai-Aktru mountain centre, a Tomsk State University (TSU) research station and a rescue post.
near: Kurai village (≈30–33 km along a dirt road/riverbed; 2 h by 4×4), Kyzyl-Tash village
elev: Alpine camp ~2,150 m (Altai-Aktru site, trofey.ru; travel companies — 2,200 m); Blue Lake 2,840 m; snout of the Maly Aktru glacier ~2,246 m, top ~3,714 m (WGMS); Aktru peak 4,044 m (other data give Aktru-Bashi 4,075 m)
short: The most accessible glacial valley in Altai: a UAZ drop from Kurai to the alpine camp at 2,150 m, from where in a day you can walk to the snouts of the Maly and Bolshoy Aktru glaciers and to Blue Lake at 2,840 m.
desc: Aktru (South Altai for “white dwelling/white house” — because of the glaciers) is a glacial basin of the North Chuya Range with 7 glaciers of a total area of about 16 km² (tonkosti); Left Bolshoy Aktru is 5.51 km² (SummitX), Maly Aktru 2.72 km², from 2,246 to 3,714 m (WGMS). Maly Aktru is a reference glacier of the World Glacier Monitoring Service (WGMS ID 795): its mass balance has been measured since 1961/62 by the TSU glacioclimatology laboratory; it is called the fastest-melting glacier in Russia, and Left Aktru, according to a TSU forecast (2019), may melt completely in the second half of the 21st century. The ice thickness in the system is up to 360 m (Altapress). The Aktru alpine camp opened in 1938 — one of the first in the USSR; before 1970 more than 2,000 badge-holders were trained here; since 1993 a search-and-rescue unit of the Emergency Ministry (MChS) has been on duty in the valley, and a year-round TSU research station operates. Today there are two complexes in the valley: the Aktru alpine camp (the old lower part — 4-person modules with stoves, VIP cottages, a banya (sauna), tent sites) and the Altai-Aktru mountain centre (the upper part — two- and three-storey houses, banyas, the Akkem cafe). Routes range from a walk through the “Gnomes’ Valley” (dwarf forest) and a visit to the snout of Maly Aktru (30 min from the trail) to Blue Lake (2,840 m), the Uchitel pass (~3,050 m), the Three Lakes Dome (3,556 m, 1B) and peaks up to grade 6A; since 2019 there has been a via ferrata on the south-eastern slope of Kyzyl-Tash peak. In the valley you can get “all four seasons in a day”. Memorials: to the climber Galina Afanasyeva and to the snowboarders killed in the 2002 helicopter crash.
guide: Leave Kurai early in the morning — clouds over the glaciers usually gather after lunch. The most rewarding day is the climb to Blue Lake at 2,840 m: the turquoise water by the Bolshoy Aktru moraine and the view of the icefall are worth it. If you have less energy, go to the snout of Maly Aktru: it is a reference glacier of the world, TSU scientists have been measuring it since 1961 and it melts faster than any in Russia, so you see it while it is still there. Find the memorial to Galina Afanasyeva — a local reminder that the mountains do not forgive mistakes. Bring a down jacket and a warm sleeping bag even in July: at night it is about +5 °C.
see: The snout of the Maly Aktru glacier; Blue Lake (2,840 m) by the Left Aktru moraine and the TSU weather station at 2,850 m; the Bolshoy Aktru icefall; the Uchitel pass (~3,050 m) with a view over the valley; the “Gnomes’ Valley” (dwarf forest); waterfalls; memorials to climbers; the via ferrata on Kyzyl-Tash; the peaks Aktru (4,044) and the Three Lakes Dome (3,556).
skip: you have only one day and no money for the vehicle drop (11–20 thousand ₽ per vehicle) — then the panorama of the range from the Kurai steppe will do. Without good footwear and readiness to walk 10–20 km a day there is little point.
diff: The valley and the snout of Maly Aktru — easy/moderate; Blue Lake — moderate (≈5 km one way from the camp, ~700 m of gain, 2.5–4 h up, a full day round trip); the Uchitel pass — moderate (5 km, up to ~3,050 m); the Three Lakes Dome 1B and above — only with training and registration with the Emergency Ministry (MChS)/KSS (control-and-rescue service).
when: July–August is the main trekking season; May is best for climbers (trofey); January–March — ice camps; the camp operates year-round. June — flood, fords on the way up.
hours: The Altai-Aktru mountain centre and the alpine camp operate year-round (sites, trofey).
daytime: Start from the camp at dawn; by lunch clouds and a risk of thunderstorms; the drop from Kurai is usually 8:00 → 10:00, back by 18:00 (seven.travel).
how: Along the Chuysky Trakt to Kurai (turn-off at about km 826), then 30–33 km south across the Kurai steppe, forest and the bed of the Tete/Aktru river: the first ~25 km to the “perevalka” (transshipment point) are passable in a prepared 4×4, the last ~8 km and ~600 m of gain only by GAZ-66, ZIL-131, KamAZ, UAZ with an experienced driver or on foot (tonkosti, trofey, NGS forum). The Kurai — camp drop takes ~2 h.
needcar: Yes: to Kurai — car/marshrutka (minibus); Kurai → Aktru — a drop in special vehicles (or on foot 8 km from the perevalka).
self: Yes, with a drop: from the camp the trails to Maly Aktru and Blue Lake are well trodden; for passes and peaks — a guide/registration. In your own car — only as far as the perevalka (a prepared 4×4).
roadtype: Paved to Kurai; then dirt across the steppe, forest, a rocky riverbed with fords (in spring the water level is high, vehicles have been swept away — NGS forum).
traveltime: Gorno-Altaysk → Kurai 6.5–8 h; Kurai → camp ~2 h (30 km) in special vehicles; camp → Blue Lake 2.5–4 h up; a side trip to Bolshoy Aktru and Blue Lake — 7–8 h (seven.travel).
stay: Altai-Aktru mountain centre (2,150 m, +7 996 962-57-84, altay-aktru.ru): houses Karatash and Maashey from 6,200 ₽, Belukha and Karagem from 6,700 ₽, Aktru and Kyzyltash 9,200 ₽ per night (site, 2026); banya 6,000 ₽/h. Aktru alpine camp (lower): 4-person modules with stoves, VIP cottages, tent sites — 2025–2026 prices not found (the alpaktru.ru site is not reachable from here). A tent in the valley — a registration fee of 150 ₽ per person (drom, 2021). In Kurai/Kyzyl-Tash — guesthouses from ~1,000 ₽, glamping 5,000–12,500 ₽.
net: not found (there is reportedly no or almost no mobile coverage in the valley — not confirmed; Wi‑Fi — ask at Altai-Aktru)
entry: No official protected-area fees found (the valley is not in a protected area per the data found); in 2021 tent groups were charged a registration fee of 150 ₽ per person (drom). Check the current amount.
transfer: Kurai ↔ Aktru: UAZ (4 seats) 11,000–20,000 ₽ per vehicle, “bukhanka” van (8) 16,000–32,000 ₽, ZIL/KamAZ (19–22) 30,000–51,000 ₽ — depending on the carrier and one way/round trip (2026). For comparison: in 2007 a GAZ-66 cost 2,500–4,500 ₽.
bring: Waterproof trekking boots, gaiters, poles, a warm sleeping bag (+5 °C at night in July), a down jacket, hat, gloves, rain jacket, sun protection and glasses (glacier), a supply of food and water, cash.
warn: Altitude 2,150–3,000+ m — altitude sickness is possible; crevasses on the glaciers — do not go onto the ice without a guide and equipment; rockfalls and sudden weather changes (snow in summer); fords on the drop in flood time. For graded routes — registration with the Emergency Ministry (MChS) (there has been a search-and-rescue post in the valley since 1993). Registration of tourist groups with the MChS is online at forms.mchs.gov.ru (processed within a day); it is not mandatory for short outings to sites by the highway, but recommended for hikes. Border zone: The border zone in the Kosh-Agach district covers only part of the territory: under FSB Order No. 282 (2006) — the Dzhazator, Mukhor-Tarkhata, Tobeler, Kazakh, Tashanta and Kokorya settlements; by FSB Order No. 512 of 13.10.2022 Mukhor-Tarkhata, Tobeler, Zhana-Aul and Kokorya were additionally removed from the zone (Tashanta, Belyashi and Argut remained in the zone). Kurai, Kyzyl-Tash, Chagan-Uzun, Aktash/Chibit (Ulagan district) are not on these lists — according to the data found, no permit is needed for this place (medium confidence: no official reply from the border directorate for this specific point was found). General rules: Russian citizens in the border zone need only a passport, a permit is required only for the 5-km strip along the border; foreigners need a permit for any point of the border zone (processing up to 60 days per the Sailyugem National Park site; 15/30 days per other sources). Where to apply: FSB border directorate for the Altai Republic, Gorno-Altaysk, 94 Kommunistichesky Ave., +7 388-22 4-82-00, pugornyjaltaj@mail.ru; branch in Kosh-Agach, 2 Armeyskaya St., +7 388-42 2-34-70. Keep your passport with you — document checks on the highway are possible. Ticks: as of 25.08.2026 the Altai Republic had 3,600 tick-bite reports and 22 cases of tick-borne encephalitis (Rospotrebnadzor) — get vaccinated/insured.
food: The Akkem cafe of the Altai-Aktru mountain centre — three meals a day for an extra fee, a hall with a fireplace and a 270° panorama (turbazy.ru, site); in Kurai — glamping cafes. Prices not found.
reviews: Yandex/2GIS ratings for the valley not found. Tours: Bolshaya Strana “Aktru Valley” — 5★; Tripster “Another Altai” — 5.0 (3 reviews). Typical pros: the closeness of the glaciers, infrastructure, views; cons: an expensive drop, a bumpy road, weather.

p.sum: The base is Kurai (km ~826 of the highway). A drop by UAZ/GAZ-66/ZIL of 30–33 km, ~2 h, 11–51 thousand ₽ per vehicle. Lodging in the valley — Altai-Aktru (from 6,200 ₽ per house) or the alpine camp/tent. The main side trips: Maly Aktru (easy), Blue Lake 2,840 m (a day), the Uchitel pass.
